You walk it to the nephew's house. She is delighted, and makes you tea in it at once.

events.text: Below a sheer red cliff, travellers shout questions and the cliff shouts back. Not the same words: other words, odd ones. A boatman says it has answered every question ever asked, and mostly wrongly.

effects.log: "Will I be great?" you shout. "Lunch!" the cliff shouts back. You decide that is fair.

ok.log: There are caves in the cliff, and in the caves, at least one very bored hermit.

fail.log: You decide it is the wind, and are wrong.

effects.log: It shouts back a better one. You row away humbled.

events.text: You climb the red cliff and find the caves. The voice belongs to an ancient hermit with a voice like a gong, who has been answering travellers for fifty years out of boredom, and now is not sure he can stop.

choices.text: Ask him to answer one honestly

effects.log: He thinks for a long time and gives you an honest answer. It is much less fun, and quite useful.

choices.text: Answer travellers with him for a day

effects.log: You shout nonsense at boats all afternoon. It is the most fun you have had in years.

events.text: The answering hermit of the red cliff has gone quiet. You climb up to find him asleep, very old, and a note on the cave wall: "Someone else must answer now. It does not matter what."

choices.text: Take his place for a season

effects.log: You answer boats for a season. A young woman asks if she should marry. "Yes!" you shout. You hope it was right.
The boats sail past in silence for the first time in fifty years. Some of them, you notice, still shout.

events.text: On a plain where a great battle was fought a lifetime ago, the wild poppies grow in long straight rows, as if planted. The farmers will not plough there. An old soldier visits every spring.
events.arc: The Field Where Flowers Grow in Rows

effects.log: He tells you where each regiment stood. The rows are the lines of the dead.
He watches you, not angry. "They will grow back," he says. "They always do."
You leave him among his rows.

events.text: The old soldier of the poppy field has a request: he wants to find the row where his best friend fell, and plant a plum tree there, but his eyes are going.
events.arc: The Field Where Flowers Grow in Rows

choices.text: Find the row from his memories

ok.log: From his story you count the rows and find it: the nineteenth, by a small stone.

fail.log: You find a row that he decides is right. It might be.

choices.text: Carry the sapling and let him lead

effects.log: He leads you by feel, by the slope of the ground. He knows.

events.text: The plum tree on the battlefield is in its first flower, a white cloud among the red poppies. The old soldier is gone, and now, every spring, other old soldiers come and plant trees of their own.
events.arc: The Field Where Flowers Grow in Rows

effects.log: You plant one. In time there is an orchard where the battle was.
The petals fall on the poppies. You stay until dark.

events.text: At the top of a high pass, so high the air is thin, a tiny post station shelters travellers. Its keeper has never been down the mountain in his life. He wants to know whether the sea is real.
events.arc: The Post Station at the Top of the World

effects.log: You describe it for an hour. He listens with his mouth open and asks if it is salty all the way down.

choices.text: Share his fire and his butter tea

effects.log: The tea is thick and salty and strange and exactly what you need.
You cross in a howling wind and are glad of the station below on the other side.

events.text: You cross the high pass again, carrying a small jar of seawater for the post station keeper. He tastes it, and coughs, and laughs until he has to sit down.
events.arc: The Post Station at the Top of the World

choices.text: Tell him more about the sea

effects.log: You tell him about tides. He thinks you are making them up. You promise you are not.

choices.text: Offer to take him down to see it

effects.log: He looks down the mountain for a long time and says, "Next year." You both know he means it this time.

events.text: The keeper of the high post station has come down from the mountain for the first time in his life. You meet him on the eastern coast, standing on the sand with his boots in his hand, staring at the sea.
events.arc: The Post Station at the Top of the World

effects.log: He watches a wave come in over his feet. He does not say anything for an hour. Neither do you.

choices.text: Take him out in a boat

effects.log: He is sick over the side twice and has the happiest day of his life.

events.text: A hermit lives in a hollow tree, and so do ten thousand bees. They do not sting him. He says they are his sect and he is their least promising disciple.

effects.log: He gives you a comb. The honey tastes of every flower on the mountain.

choices.text: Sit very still near the bees

effects.log: They land on your arms and walk about. None of them sting. You hardly breathe.
You keep a sensible distance. A bee follows you down the hill, curious.

events.text: The bee hermit's bees are swarming: the queen has left the hollow tree, and ten thousand bees hang from a branch in a great humming ball. He needs someone calm to carry them to a new home.

ok.log: You carry the humming ball in a basket up the mountain. Not one sting. The hermit bows to you.

fail.log: Three stings. Only three. The hermit says that is a compliment from bees.

choices.text: Hold the basket while he does it

effects.log: You hold the basket. He talks to the bees the whole time, very politely.

events.text: The bee hermit has died, and the bees have stayed in the hollow tree. When you visit, they come out and hang in the air around you, humming, as if waiting for something.

effects.log: You tell them he has died, the old way. They hum lower, then go back in. In spring there is honey on the hermit's grave.
You sit by the tree every day for a summer. You are their least promising disciple now.

events.text: In a windy mountain pass, an old kite maker builds kites as big as houses and flies them on ropes thick as your wrist. He says, one day, one will carry him across the gorge.
events.arc: The Kite Maker of the Pass

effects.log: It takes six of you to hold the rope. The kite pulls like a tethered dragon.

choices.text: Ask how far he has got

effects.log: "Halfway," he says, and shows you a scar.
"Yes," he agrees, delighted.

events.text: The kite maker's greatest kite is ready: red silk on bamboo, long as a temple hall. Today the wind is right. He wants you on the rope, because, he says, you are the only one who will not let go.
events.arc: The Kite Maker of the Pass

ok.log: You hold. He rises into the wind across the gorge, shouting, and lands on the far side in a heap, laughing.

fail.log: The rope burns your hands, but you do not let go. He lands short, in a pine tree, unhurt and ecstatic.

choices.text: Talk him into tying a safety line

effects.log: He grumbles and ties it. He flies halfway and is hauled back, beaming.

events.text: The village in the pass has a kite festival now, in honour of the kite maker who flew. Children fly little red kites. The old man sits at the top of the pass in a chair, directing everyone.
events.arc: The Kite Maker of the Pass

choices.text: Fly a kite with the children

effects.log: Your kite goes higher than anyone's. The old man claps.

choices.text: Ask him what it felt like

effects.log: "Like being forgiven," he says, "for everything at once." You think about that for a long time.

events.text: In a roadside teahouse a blind old man pours tea without spilling a drop, and when a drunk knocks a cup off the table he catches it without looking. The drunk goes very quiet.
events.arc: The Blind Swordsman of the Teahouse

effects.log: He pours for you. "You walk like someone who trains," he says. "Badly, but often."

choices.text: Test him with a flicked coin

ok.log: He catches it between two fingers and puts it in the tip jar. You both laugh.

fail.log: He catches it, and flicks it back. It hits you on the nose.

effects.log: You leave. Some masters prefer to be teahouse owners.

events.text: Bandits come to the blind master's teahouse to rob the till. He goes on pouring tea. One of them draws a blade and puts it to his throat. The old man sighs.
events.arc: The Blind Swordsman of the Teahouse

ok.log: You and the old man together, him with a teapot, you with your fists. It is over in a breath.

fail.log: You are knocked down. The old man finishes it with a tea tray, then helps you up.

effects.log: He does not stand up. Four bandits are on the floor. Not a drop of tea is spilled.

events.text: The blind master of the teahouse has decided you are worth teaching, a little. He blindfolds you and pours tea, and you must catch the cup when he drops it.
events.arc: The Blind Swordsman of the Teahouse

ok.log: After a hundred broken cups, you catch one. He laughs. "Now you can hear," he says.

fail.log: You break fifty cups. He sighs and keeps pouring. One day, he says.

choices.text: Ask why he never said he was a master

effects.log: "I am a tea seller," he says. "The other thing is just something I can do."

events.text: At an inn on a pass, every guest wakes up having dreamed the same dream: a garden with a white gate. Nobody knows why. The innkeeper says it has been so for a hundred years and is very good for business.
events.arc: The Inn Where Everyone Dreams the Same

effects.log: You dream it: a garden, a white gate, someone humming behind it.
A merchant, a monk, a soldier: the same gate, the same humming.
You dream of horses. The innkeeper is offended.

events.text: You dream of the white gate again at the inn on the pass. This time it is open. A very old woman is pruning roses in the garden and looks up at you. "Finally," she says. "Someone who comes in."
events.arc: The Inn Where Everyone Dreams the Same

effects.log: You walk the garden in the dream. She shows you every rose and tells you each one is a guest who dreamed here.
"The innkeeper's grandmother," she says. "I wanted company. A hundred years is a long time to garden alone."

events.text: You tell the innkeeper about his grandmother's garden in the dream. He goes very quiet, and takes you behind the inn, to a wild corner full of brambles where there is, rotting and grey, a white gate.
events.arc: The Inn Where Everyone Dreams the Same

effects.log: You clear it together in a season. Roses come back. Nobody at the inn dreams the dream again; they do not need to.
You plant one. That night you dream of her once more. She waves, and closes the gate.

events.text: High in the winter mountains you find a hot spring steaming among snowy rocks. It is full of monkeys. They look at you as if you are a very rude guest.
events.arc: The Hot Spring in the Snow

effects.log: After a long negotiation of stares, they let you have a corner. The heat melts a year out of your bones.
You wait in the snow until they leave. It takes all afternoon. The water is worth it.
They splash you back, harder. You lose, and retreat, dripping.

events.text: You come back to the monkeys' hot spring. A young monkey is stuck on an ice ledge above the steaming water, crying, and the troop is screaming at you as if it is your fault.
events.arc: The Hot Spring in the Snow

ok.log: You climb the ice and bring it down in your arms. The troop goes silent and lets you into the best spot.

fail.log: You slip into the spring with the monkey in your arms. You are both soaked and safe. The troop is pleased anyway.

effects.log: It grabs the branch and scrambles down. Its mother glares at you, then grooms your sleeve.

events.text: When you come to the hot spring now, the monkeys make room. The young one you saved, grown, sits next to you in the steam and picks the snow out of your hair, very seriously.
events.arc: The Hot Spring in the Snow

effects.log: Snow falls, steam rises, a monkey grooms your hair. Your qi has never been so calm.
The whole troop crowds in. You run out in a breath. They are very forgiving.

events.text: A village on a river holds a festival every year to marry a straw doll to the river god, so he will not flood the fields. This year the shaman says the god wants a real bride. The village is arguing about whose daughter.

effects.log: You stand up in the square and call it murder. The square goes quiet, then splits in half.

choices.text: Ask to talk to the river god yourself

effects.log: The shaman laughs. Then he sees you are serious, and stops laughing.
You find he has been paid by a landlord who wants the girls' families' land.

events.text: On the night of the river god's wedding, the village gathers on the bank. The shaman stands at the water with a garlanded boat. You are there.

ok.log: You throw the shaman into the river instead. He floats. The god, it seems, does not want him either.

fail.log: His men hold you back, but in the struggle the boat floats away empty, and the village takes that as the god's answer.

choices.text: Offer yourself instead, and walk in

effects.log: You walk into the river up to your chest and say the god has refused you. The village decides that settles it.

events.text: The village on the river has gone back to marrying a straw doll to the river god, and the festival is happier than it has been in years. The shaman is gone. The river has not flooded.

effects.log: You weave her a fine straw dress. The village girls laugh at your clumsy fingers.

choices.text: Help them build a better dyke

effects.log: You spend a month on the dyke. Next spring the river rises and stops, politely, at the stones.

events.text: On the highest ridge of the western mountains, where no tree grows, a single snow lotus is blooming on a ledge: the flower that, they say, blooms once in a hundred years and can mend any wound of the meridians.

effects.log: You look at it for an hour. White petals, a gold heart, in the middle of all that ice.

ok.log: You reach the ledge and pick it. It is cold as snow, and smells of nothing at all.

fail.log: The ledge breaks. You get back by a hair, with nothing.

effects.log: You mark the ridge in your memory. Someone may need it more than you, one day.

events.text: In a town far below the snow ridge, a young martial artist lies paralysed, meridians shattered in a duel. Healers say only a snow lotus could mend them. The family is selling everything to send someone up the mountain.

effects.log: You draw the family a map. Their eldest son climbs it, and comes back with it, and weeps on your doorstep.

choices.text: Climb up and bring them the lotus

effects.log: You climb to the ledge and back, a month of ice and wind. The young one walks again by spring.

events.text: The snow lotus you picked has not wilted. It sits in a cup of snow water on your table, as fresh as on the ridge. You know now what it is for. In a town far below, someone needs it.

effects.log: You walk it down to the healer. A young fighter walks again. The lotus, when it is used, smells at last: of snow and gratitude.

choices.text: Keep it for your own need

effects.log: You keep it. One day you will be glad of it, or someone close to you will.
